newsitem.title: FRANCE: French budget in no way hurts growth - Arthuis.
newsitem.headline: French budget in no way hurts growth - Arthuis.

text.p: Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told his fellow deputies in the UDF political group on Tuesday that the 1997 budget presented last week would in no way suffocate economic growth.
"In no way is this a growth-inhibiting budget," he told his political allies at a meeting in this seaside resort town.
"We're heading in the right direction. We're set on a course of confidence, growth and employment."
Let's stick to this course and the discussion on this finance bill should allow us to convince our fellow countrymen we're headed in the right direction."
Arthuis said in a rallying call that the 1997 budget was a "historic" one.

The budget, presented last Wednesday, seeks to limit central government spending to 1996 levels of 1,552 billion francs and in reality means 60 billions in savings and windfalls to make up for the automatic rise that would result from inflation and other mechanical increments.
"Go ahead and say it's a good budget," Arthuis said.
There would be a meeting at the finance ministry next week to spell out the rationale of the 1997 budget to deputies from the ruling majority, he added.

Arthuis defended the rise in petrol excise duties in the budget, in response to a question from deputy Jean-Pierre Thomas from the Republican Party, which is part of the UDF group, which is in turn junior partner in the ruling centre-right coalition.
"There has never been such a limited rise as the one we're proposing," he said. "Six centimes is infinitely smaller than has been the case in recent years."
"We would have been delighted if we could have presented a budget which cut all kinds of taxes," he said. "
